newsitem.title: USA: Clinton says U.S. helping Iraqi dissidents flee.
newsitem.headline: Clinton says U.S. helping Iraqi dissidents flee.

text.p: The United States is helping Americans and "those who have worked with us" to flee Iraq as fighting between Kurdish factions in northern Iraq continues, President Bill Clinton said on Monday.
"We're doing everything we think we can to help anyone who needs to be out of Iraq," Clinton told reporters after an Oval Office ceremony concerning aviation safety.

Clinton declined to elaborate, but his comments came in response to a question about some 200 Iraqi Arabs with links to the U.S. Central Intelligence Agency who reportedly fled Arbil after Iraqi troops stormed the Kurdish city last week.
The Washington Post reported on Monday that these opponents of Iraqi President Saddam Hussein are holed up in a mountain hideaway in northern Iraq hoping for U.S. political asylum.
"We're doing everything we can to get out of Iraq American citizens and those who have worked with us," Clinton said.
He added that the United States was also warning Kurdish forces fighting in the region "that there should not be any cavalier killing of civilians and others who are not combatants in this."
